_doc: barks.json (AI-A). One-liners spoken in bubbles. Top-level keys are groups; every leaf is a non-empty array of strings. Pick a line with the seeded RNG. Placeholders (optional, replace before display): {item} = lowercase item name ('red mitten'), {car} = car name ('the Dining car'), {name} = speaker's first name. Groups: ambient.<routine> (reading|napping|eating|staring|chatting|kids|vendor|conductor|boarding|leaving) = scenery chatter; claimant_intro.<mood> = first line when a claimant arrives (calm|hurried|worried|shy|grumpy), all use {item}; waiting.<mood> = said while the claimant waits for the attendant; thanks.<mood> = correct handover; wrong.<mood> = 'not mine' reaction; refused.imposter = said by an imposter when refused; refused.honest = said by an honest claimant wrongly refused; attendant.idle = Bram-free mutters for the attendant avatar; station.announce = tannoy lines at arrival (use {stop}). Keys are stable: add lines freely, never rename keys. AI-C additions: station.stops.<stop name> = 2 arrival lines per stop in routes.json (use after station.announce, e.g. Content.lines('barks',['station','stops',name])); tutorial.<stage> = hint text per Sim.get_tutorial stage (find_item,to_bench,examine,hand_over,sweep) + bram_after toast.

reading: Chapter eleven. Everyone is lying in chapter eleven.
I have read this sentence four times. It is still about a goose.
Do not tell me how it ends. I'm cheating and reading the middle.
This book is damp. I don't want to talk about it.
Shh. The detective is about to say something obvious.
Page two hundred. Page two hundred and one. Page two hundred.
Lovely story. Far too many sheep.
I've read this page four times. It's still the best page.
The butler did it. Or the vicar. The page is damp.
Shh, the detective's about to explain everything.
Somebody's folded down the best part. I forgive them.
Chapter twelve is shorter. Chapter twelve is a lie.
I'd read the ending, but the train might end first.
napping: Wake me at the sea. Not before.
Zzz... I did return the library book... zzz...
Don't mind me. I'm resting my eyes. Both of them.
Zzz... it was a very large biscuit...
Mhm... tell the moon I'll be right there...
Five more stops. Wake me for pudding.
I wasn't sleeping. I was resting my eyes, loudly.
Mm. The wheels sing the best lullabies.
No, no, I'm awake. I'm only dreaming with my eyes shut.
Zzz... tell the cat it's fine...
If I snore, it's the train. It's always the train.
eating: I ordered soup. This is a sandwich. I'm not complaining.
Crumbs. Everywhere. It's a travelling feast.
Is it rude to dunk toast in the tea? Asking for me.
One more sausage roll and then I'm a sensible person.
The jam is on the wrong side of the plate. I like it.
Do not look at my pudding. It's shy.
This sandwich has seen more stops than I have.
A crumb for the pigeon, a crumb for me.
Tea, toast, and a very long view. Perfect.
Someone's made soup in a flask. Heroic.
I saved the best bit for last, and then ate it first.
Pie by lamplight tastes twice as good.
staring: The moon's keeping up with us again.
I always count the lamp posts. I lose count at nine.
Somebody's light is on in that farmhouse. Somebody's waiting up.
Fog's coming in. Cosy, isn't it?
That hill looks like a sleeping cat.
Every window is a tiny film.
I wonder who lives in the lighthouse. Gulls, mostly.
The moon is keeping pace. Polite of it.
Is that a hill, or a very large sleeping dog?
I could watch the dark go by all night. And I do.
There's a light in that window. Someone's up late, like us.
Every station's a little stage. Somebody's always waiting.
The glass is cold. The view is warm. Funny.
chatting: And then she said, 'It's not a hat, it's a nest.'
No, no, you said Tuesday. It was definitely Tuesday.
Did you pack the umbrella? The other umbrella?
He told me the conductor is three conductors in a trench coat.
I'm only saying the tea was better last year.
Wait, wait, say it again, slower.
You never told me you could whistle!
We should have brought a map. Or a goat. Something useful.
No, I said the soup was hot, not the soup was *sad*.
She tipped her hat and I tipped mine. We've not spoken since.
I'm only saying, a train should have a map.
He told me it was a secret. So of course I told everyone.
We've met before. Or I've met someone very like you.
And that's when the lamp went out. Spooky, no? It was just the lamp.
kids: Mum! The train is breathing on the window!
I drew a face in the fog. It's you.
Bet I can see the sea first.
Are we there? Are we there yet? What about now?
I'm not looking at anything. I'm looking at everything.
The moon is following us. I checked.
Can the train go faster? Just a bit? Politely?
I found a button! It's mine now. It's a lucky button.
Are we nearly there? Are we nearly nearly?
I'm going to count all the stars. I'm up to six.
The train waved at me! With its steam!
I found a button. Is it mine? It's mine now.
Mum, is the moon following us or are we following the moon?
vendor: Pasties! Warm pasties! Don't ask what's in them!
Sweets for the sweet and sweets for the sour!
Tea, madam? Tea, sir? Tea, small gentleman?
Sandwiches, cut on the diagonal, as nature intended!
Mind your toes, I'm a trolley with ambitions.
Hot chestnuts! Hotter than the Dining car!
Lemonade! Sour enough to wake the conductor!
Tea! Strong enough to hold the spoon up!
Postcards of every stop! Some of them accurate!
conductor: Tickets, please. Tickets, kindly. Tickets, if you've a moment.
Mind the gap. It's gotten bigger overnight.
Nothing to see in the next car. Plenty to see in this one.
Punctual to the minute. Give or take eleven.
Everything is in hand. Mostly mine.
Evening, attendant. Anything interesting under the seats?
The line is long and the night is longer.
Mind the step. Mind the other step.
All tickets are valid, if you believe in them.
I punch holes in tickets and, occasionally, in rumours.
Anyone lost? The Lost Property car is just down there. Mind the lamp.
The train will arrive when the train arrives.
boarding: Is this the right train? It feels right.
Pardon me. Excuse me. Coming through with a suitcase.
Window seat, please, window seat, window seat.
Platform Zero? Never heard of it. I love it.
Just made it! My coat wasn't so lucky.
Is anyone sitting here? Is anything sitting here?
Room for one more? I travel light. Mostly regrets.
I'm sure I had a ticket. It's somewhere. Probably.
This feels like the right train. It feels like it's been waiting.
Mind my bag. It's full of other people's umbrellas.
leaving: Mind the step. It minds me.
Home at last. Or a version of home.
Off I pop. Don't wait up.
Whoever took my seat, enjoy it. It's lumpy.
Thank you for having me. Mind my seat, it's warm.
That's my stop. I think. I hope. It's lovely, anyway.
Safe travels. Keep your things close.
rain: Listen to the rain on the roof. Best seat in the house.
Wet tracks, warm lamps. I'll take it.
Every drop thinks it's the only one. Charming.
Rain's good for a story. Not so good for a hat.
snow: Snow! The whole world's gone quiet and polite.
The window's frosted over. Someone's drawn a very small train.
Every flake's different. I've not checked them all.
fog: Fog. The train's feeling its way, like a cat.
I can't see the platform. I can feel it, though.
Everything's soft in fog. Even the signals look sleepy.
Is that a station, or a cloud with ambition?
late_night: It's very late, or very early. Same train either way.
Everyone's quieter after midnight. Even the wheels.
Night shift on the Zero Line. Tea's on me.
Past midnight the lamps seem to hum together.

calm: Evening. I've lost my {item}. No rush at all.
Hello there. I believe my {item} wandered off.
Excuse me, attendant. A {item}, if one's turned up?
Good evening. Missing: one {item}. Not urgently.
I seem to have mislaid my {item}. Happens.
Might you have my {item}? It's a pleasant sort of thing.
Hallo. I'm after a {item}. I'll wait if I must.
Nice night for it. Anyone hand in a {item}?
hurried: My {item}! Have you got my {item}? I've a connection!
Quick, quick, {item}, lost it, need it, please!
Don't mean to rush you, but, {item}, now, thank you!
{item}, {item}, {item}. You'd know it if you saw it. Hurry!
I'm due at the next stop. Lost a {item}. Go, go, go!
Sorry, sorry, short on time, one {item}, anyone?
I've got ninety seconds and one missing {item}.
Lost property? Good. Lost {item}. Go!
worried: Oh dear, oh dear, my {item}. Please say you have it.
I can't find my {item} anywhere. I looked. I looked twice.
It meant so much. My {item}. Please, has anyone...?
I think I left my {item} somewhere. I'm sure I did. Maybe.
Oh, thank goodness you're here. I've lost my {item}.
If it's gone, it's gone, but, my {item}, is it...?
I had it just a moment ago, my {item}. Truly.
Please tell me my {item} has turned up. I'll be ever so quiet.
shy: Um. Sorry. I, um, lost a {item}?
Hi. It's small. The {item}. I don't want to be a bother.
I wasn't sure if I should... but my {item}...
Sorry to ask. Has a {item} been handed in? ...Sorry.
Er. Hello. A {item}. It's, um. Mine. Was.
I'll just stand here. If you happen to have a {item}...
Don't mind me. Only a {item}. Probably nothing.
I lost my {item}. I practised saying that. It went better.
grumpy: Somebody's nicked my {item}. Where is it?
My {item}. Missing. This is a disgrace.
Lost property, is it? Then find my {item}.
I want my {item}. I'm not asking twice. I'm asking once, loudly.
Hmph. A {item}. I had one. Now I don't. Explain.
Don't smile. Where's my {item}?
If I find out who touched my {item}, there'll be words.
I've been looking for my {item} since the last tunnel.

calm: Take your time. I'm only a person.
Mm. Lovely lamp you've got.
No hurry. The train isn't going anywhere. It is, but still.
I'll just admire the shelves.
hurried: Tick tock, attendant, tick tock.
Is it that one? That one? That one?
I can hear the next station coming.
Hurry! Respectfully!
worried: Oh, what if it isn't there?
I'm sure it's fine. It's fine. Is it fine?
Please, please, please.
I've got a feeling about this. Mostly nerves.
shy: I'll just be over here. Being small.
Don't look at me. Look at the shelves.
grumpy: I'm still here, you know.
Hmph. Slow service on a fast train.
My feet are developing opinions.
Are we doing this or are we sightseeing?

calm: That's the one. Thank you kindly.
Lovely. You're a credit to the car.
Perfect. Evening restored.
Wonderful. I'll sleep well tonight.
hurried: Yes! Thanks! Bye! Wonderful! Bye!
You're a marvel! I'm running!
Got it! Thank you! Gone!
Brilliant! Don't tell my watch!
worried: Oh, thank goodness. I could hug you. May I? No. Thank you.
You found it. You actually found it. Oh.
My heart can start again. Thank you.
I knew it. I didn't know it. Thank you!
shy: Oh! Thank you. Really. Thank you.
That's... yes. Thank you. Sorry. Thank you.
You're very kind. I'll go now. Thank you.
Mine! I mean. Yes. Thank you.
grumpy: Hmph. About time. Thank you, I suppose.
That'll do. That'll do nicely, actually.
Well. Fine. You're not entirely hopeless.
Good. Don't let it happen again. To me. Or anyone.

calm: Ah, no, that isn't mine, I'm afraid.
Close, though. A different sort of close.
Hmm. That belongs to someone with better taste. Mine's lovelier.
No, that's not it, but thank you for trying.
hurried: No! Not that! Another! Quick!
That's the wrong one! I'm sure! Try again!
Not mine! Not even slightly! Faster!
Argh, no, other one, other one!
worried: Oh. No. That's not mine. Oh dear.
I don't think so. I'm so sorry. Is there another?
It looks like it, but... no. No. Sorry.
Oh no. It isn't. Is it? It isn't.
shy: Um, sorry, I don't think that's mine...
Ah. No. Sorry. Thank you anyway.
grumpy: That's not mine. Are you blind or merely fast?
Wrong. Next.
Not mine. I'd know. I always know.
Is that supposed to be funny?

imposter: Well! I never! Fine. Keep your old thing.
Hmph. It was worth a try. I mean. It was mine!
I... really thought that was it. I was mistaken. Entirely mistaken.
Hm. Perhaps I mixed it up with another. A completely hypothetical other.
Fine, fine. No need for the eyebrow.
honest: Oh. I was sure that was mine. I'm sorry to have bothered you.
Hmm. Perhaps I misremember. I'll look again.
Right. Sorry. I'll be on my way.

idle: One more tag. One more story.
The lamp hums. The wheels hum back.
Somewhere a glove is missing a friend.
Right. Where did I put the magnifier?
Brass polishes itself if you ignore it long enough. Not true.
Three tags, two mysteries, one kettle.
The night shift never ends. It just changes stations.

announce: Now arriving at {stop}. Please mind your belongings.
{stop}. Doors on both sides. Hats on heads.
This is {stop}. Check under your seat. Then check again.
{stop}, ladies and gentlemen. Lost something? You know where I am.
Next stop, {stop}. Items left behind are in safe hands.
{stop}. Change here for nothing in particular.
{stop} now. Take everything you came with. Or at least most of it.

Platform Zero: Platform Zero. Where it begins, if it begins. Mind the gap and the nostalgia.
Platform Zero, the first stop and possibly the last. Do check you have all your things.
Lantern Junction: Lantern Junction. Every lamp here was lit by hand. Please admire them quietly.
Now arriving at Lantern Junction. The porters are kind and the kettle is on.
Saltmarsh Halt: Saltmarsh Halt. Smells of rain and old rope. Wellingtons are not provided.
Saltmarsh Halt, where the gulls collect the tickets. Do not feed them yours.
Pinewick: Pinewick. The pines have been waiting a long while and are patient about it.
Pinewick station. Please stamp the snow from your boots, and any worries with it.
Cold Spoon Pass: Cold Spoon Pass. Mind the frost. Mind the spoon-shaped moon.
Cold Spoon Pass. The tea here freezes in the pot. The company does not.
Marigold Crossing: Marigold Crossing. A field of orange in the dark, if you squint, which you may.
Marigold Crossing. Passengers for nowhere in particular, this is your stop.
Brasswater: Brasswater. Mind the puddles, they reflect better than you'd think.
Brasswater, the town that polished its own rain. Welcome, or welcome back.
Gull's Rest: Gull's Rest. A long, quiet halt by the sea. Take your time. The train will.
Gull's Rest. Please do not tell the gulls where you keep your sandwiches.
Hollow Birch: Hollow Birch. Mind the owls. They have opinions about luggage.
Hollow Birch. The trees here keep secrets. Please keep yours too.
Tuppence Hill: Tuppence Hill. Cheap views, priceless sky. Please check under your seats.
Tuppence Hill. If you find a coin, it's lost property. If you find two, it's a mystery.
Frostmere: Frostmere. A frozen lake, a long dwell, and a very strong tea.
Frostmere. Mind the ice. Mind the silence. It's the good sort.
Ember Street: Ember Street. Warm windows all the way down. Someone's baking, and it's not you.
Ember Street, last of the loop and first of the next. Please collect your belongings.

find_item: Something warm is in the bin. Go and have a look.
There's a rustle in the bin by the window. Tap to walk there.
to_bench: Carry it to the bench. Tools live there.
Lamp-light's best at the bench. Take it over.
examine: Pick a tool. Every little thing is a clue.
Try the magnifier, or the lamp. Smells and sounds count too.
hand_over: Bram's waiting. Take it to the counter and hand it over.
That fits what he said. Take it to the counter.
sweep: Well done. Now sweep the passenger car. People leave things everywhere.
The passenger car has things nobody's claimed yet. Go look.
bram_after: Bram grins, black-handed and delighted. 'Tea in the engine room, any time.'
Bram tips an imaginary hat. 'You've the knack, attendant.'

intro: Tonight's case comes in on the night post. Someone is missing something.
A new case, wrapped in brown paper and mystery.
The Night Case is on the bench. The lamp is warm. Shall we?
Someone's lost something dear, and left a note. A thin one.
Same train, same lamp, a different puzzle.
solved: Case closed. The owner left whistling.
That's the one. Quietly, a small miracle.
You've done it. The lamp seems brighter.
Handed over, thanked, and gone into the night.
Another thing found. Another small relief.
share_flavor: The Zero Line never loses a thing for good.
One more lost thing, home safe.
Nothing is truly lost on the Zero Line.
